mt: 'WIKIDATA' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE KNOWLEDGE GRAPH AT ITS DATA MODEL; ITS OWN Q-NUMBERS GIVEN, ITS ROLE AS HUB OF THE NAME AUTHORITIES (ISNI, VIAF, ORCID) AND ITS PSEUDONYM PROPERTY NOT CARRIED
d: THE KNOWLEDGE BASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'Wikidata is a free, open, and collaborative multilingual knowledge graph hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation. It serves as a central storage hub for structured data used by Wikipedia, Wikimedia sister projects, and external applications.' Key Features: CC0 ('All data is released'); 'Q-number' items ('`Q42` for Douglas Adams') and P-numbers ('`P69` for "educated at"'); statements and triples with references; multilingual labels, descriptions and aliases; the SPARQL Query Service. Eight cards: Wikidata (two), Wikipedia, the Query Service, GitHub, three YouTube videos.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the name, the Overview introduces the knowledge base as a newcomer would meet it: host, license, how items and statements work, and how to query.
findings: THE DATA MODEL AT ITS GRAIN. Statements 'link entities to values, often backed by references to external sources', and labels, descriptions and aliases 'exist across hundreds of languages'. The introduction: 'The Wikidata repository consists mainly of items , each one having a label , a description and any number of aliases .' and 'Wikidata records not just statements, but also their sources, and connections to other databases.' The host is right ('hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation'); Wikimedia Deutschland, the editors 'who decide on the rules of content creation and management', the bots, the launch of 29 October 2012 and the count ('more than 123 million data entities') are not carried.

THE LICENSE WIDENED. 'All data is released under a Creative Commons CC0 public domain dedication'. The introduction limits it: 'All structured data from the main, Property, Lexeme, and EntitySchema namespaces is available under the Creative Commons CC0 License ; text in the other namespaces is available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike License'.

THE HUB OF NAMES NOT CARRIED. The composition gives Wikidata's internal identifiers ('Q42', 'P69') and no external one. The census row's interest is the other kind: 'A property that links an item to an external database, such as an authority control database used by libraries and archives, is called an identifier', with 'ISNI (P213)', VIAF numbers 'incorporated into Wikidata', and 'Both Wikipedia and Wikidata include pages with ORCID identifiers' in the saved sources. The pseudonym property is absent too: 'pseudonym (P742)', 'alias used by someone', whose aliases run 'pen name stage name code name user name known professionally as heteronym nom de plume', with 'Data type String'. 'Aliases' is the composition's only word for a second name.
analysis: The knowledge base composed accurately as a data model and a query service, with its license stated wider than its own page states it. The two features that make it a census row, the identifier properties that join ISNI, VIAF and ORCID, and the property that stores a heteronym as a string on its bearer's item, are absent.
per_note: The Wikimedia Foundation named as host; internal identifiers (Q42, P69) given; sources carded.

evidence.record_quote: Wikidata is a free , collaborative , multilingual , secondary knowledge base, collecting structured data to provide support for Wikipedia , Wikimedia Commons , the other wikis of the Wikimedia movement , and to anyone in the world.

atoms.reference: Hosted and owned by the Wikimedia Foundation, developed mainly by Wikimedia Deutschland; data entered and maintained by editors, who decide the rules of content, and by bots.

evidence.record_quote: Wikidata is a collaboratively edited multilingual knowledge graph hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation .
Launched in October 2012, it is developed mainly by Wikimedia Deutschland
Data is entered and maintained by Wikidata editors, who decide on the rules of content creation and management. Automated bots also enter data into Wikidata.

atoms.reference: Items, each with a label, a description and aliases, described by statements of a property and a value, recorded with their sources and connections to other databases.

evidence.record_quote: The Wikidata repository consists mainly of items , each one having a label , a description and any number of aliases .
Statements describe detailed characteristics of an Item and consist of a property and a value .
Wikidata records not just statements, but also their sources, and connections to other databases.

atoms.reference: More than 123 million data entities; items for scholarly articles the largest part, followed by biographies.

evidence.record_quote: Wikidata held more than 123 million data entities, such as items, properties and lexemes.
Items for scholarly articles are the biggest part of Wikidata, followed by the collection of biographies.

atoms.reference: A free, collaborative, multilingual, secondary knowledge base collecting structured data to support Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, the other Wikimedia wikis and anyone in the world.

evidence.record_quote: Wikidata is a free , collaborative , multilingual , secondary knowledge base, collecting structured data to provide support for Wikipedia , Wikimedia Commons , the other wikis of the Wikimedia movement , and to anyone in the world.

atoms.reference: Structured data in the main, Property, Lexeme and EntitySchema namespaces under CC0, reusable even commercially without permission; text in other namespaces under CC BY-SA.

evidence.record_quote: All structured data from the main, Property, Lexeme, and EntitySchema namespaces is available under the Creative Commons CC0 License ; text in the other namespaces is available under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike License
You can copy, modify, distribute and perform the data, even for commercial purposes, without asking for permission.

atoms.reference: A property linking an item to an external database such as a library authority file is an identifier; Wikidata carries ISNI (P213), VIAF numbers and ORCID identifiers.

evidence.record_quote: A property that links an item to an external database, such as an authority control database used by libraries and archives, is called an identifier .
The file numbers are also being added to Wikipedia biographical articles and are incorporated into Wikidata .
Both Wikipedia and Wikidata include pages with ORCID identifiers.
